description:
Project: “Incident bot + diagnostics improvements” (Reliability Program)

Goals
- Reduce MTTR and incident toil by improving automated context gathering during incidents and high-severity alerts.
- Make the incident bot immediately useful in the first 2–5 minutes of triage by attaching the most relevant, time-bounded evidence:
  - Recent deploys/rollouts (service, version, region, canary status, change links)
  - Config diffs (feature flags, routing policies, rate limits, autoscaling knobs)
  - Saturation signals (GPU/CPU/memory, queue depth, throttling, token/second capacity, scheduler contention)
- Increase reliability outcomes via better early detection and safer mitigations (graceful degradation, circuit breakers, automated rollback recommendations).

Scope
- Incident bot
  - New “context bundles” posted automatically to #incidents threads and linked into postmortems.
  - Pluggable collectors (deploy collector, config diff collector, saturation collector).
  - Guardrails: timeouts, sampling, redaction, and restricted visibility for customer-sensitive data.
- Diagnostics improvements
  - Standardize and improve key operational signals: saturation metrics, per-model/per-route SLO indicators, recent change annotations.
  - Better correlation: trace/log links, deployment events, config changes, and error spikes.
- Integrations
  - GitHub (PR/deploy links), CI/CD and release events, configuration store (policy bundle / feature flags), observability stack (dashboards/alerts), and on-call tooling.

Out of scope (initial phases)
- Full auto-mitigation (bot executing remediations) beyond suggesting runbook steps and surfacing safe rollback candidates.
- Customer-facing UX changes in Console beyond adding reliable annotations and links used by responders.

Stakeholders & teams
- Eng SRE (ownership of incident workflow, paging hygiene, incident bot behavior): Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton, Aisha Bello.
- Platform / Control plane & routing (config diffs, rollout and routing policy context): Priya Natarajan’s org.
- Observability (signal definitions, dashboards, tracing/metrics pipelines): Allison Grant, Logan Wright’s telemetry org.
- Product (Console & Rollouts requirements, prioritization, rollout communication): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes.
- Infra / Release engineering (deploy event sources, metadata consistency): Eng Infra + Eng Releases.

Timeline (illustrative)
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): requirements + top incident patterns, define “minimum useful context bundle”, baseline MTTR/toil metrics.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): recent deploy collector + deploy annotations in incident threads; add links to dashboards/runbooks.
- Phase 2 (3–5 weeks): config diff collector (routing policies/flags) with redaction + audit trails.
- Phase 3 (3–6 weeks): saturation collector + standardized saturation dashboards/alerts; tie into graceful degradation guidance.
- Phase 4 (2–3 weeks): rollout/canary support, performance and reliability hardening, documentation, and post-launch review.

Key deliverables
- Confluence: design/ADR, operational runbooks, SLO/error-budget updates, incident-process updates.
- Linear: project plan, scoped issues, dependencies, rollout tasks, acceptance criteria.
- GitHub PRs: incident-bot collectors, APIs, tests, dashboards/config additions, rollout flags.
- Slack: incident threads where the bot is iterated on, feedback loops from on-call.
- Drive: working notes, incident taxonomy, metrics baselines, and rollout checklists.
- Jira (support): a small number of customer-facing incidents/escalations used as motivating examples and validation cases.

Constraints
- Data sensitivity: avoid posting customer payloads/tokens; strict redaction and restricted channels where needed.
- Reliability: collectors must fail open (never block incident flow), with bounded latency and predictable load.
- Cardinality/scale: saturation and correlation signals must be engineered to avoid high-cardinality metric explosions.
- Multi-region correctness: deploy/config context must be region-aware and time-synchronized.

files.description: Published spec for “context bundles”: what the incident bot posts, ordering, time windows, redaction rules, and example outputs. Includes required data sources and failure-mode behavior.
ADR covering plugin/collector architecture (interfaces, timeouts, caching, retries), rationale vs monolith, and how new collectors are added and tested.
Standard definitions for saturation signals (GPU utilization vs SM occupancy, queue depth, scheduler contention, KV cache pressure), required labels, and recommended alert thresholds.
Updates to incident process: how responders should use bot context bundles, when to request deeper diagnostics, and how to report false positives/irrelevant context.
Runbook that starts from deploy + config diff evidence (roll back, disable flag, revert routing change), with decision tree and links to dashboards/log queries.
Dashboard spec: change annotations (deploys/config) overlaid on error/latency graphs; includes example panels and required event schema.
Defines how this project will be measured: MTTR deltas, time-to-suspect-change, on-call toil reduction, bot latency/error rates, and adoption metrics.
Postmortem focused on missing early context (recent deploy/config changes and saturation clues). Serves as a motivating case and source of requirements for collectors.
Linear project seed issue: Incident bot + diagnostics improvements (scope, milestones, success metrics, owners, and initial task breakdown).
Implement deploy collector: fetch last N deploys per service/region, link to GitHub PRs and release pipeline runs, and post a concise summary into incident threads.
Implement config diff collector: compare effective routing/policy config between t-30m and now; include redaction and “safe to post” classification.
Saturation collector v1: compute and post saturation snapshot (GPU queue depth, throttling, scheduler contention) with links to canonical dashboards.
Incident bot reliability hardening: timeouts, circuit breakers, caching, and graceful degradation of collectors (partial bundle with clear error messaging).
Event schema for deploy/config annotations: define and implement a consistent event payload used by dashboards and bot collectors.
Add bot posting controls: per-channel allowlist, restricted visibility mode for sensitive incidents, and redaction audit logs.
Backfill and validate saturation metrics quality: check cardinality, missing labels, and correlate with real incidents; includes a testing plan and rollout steps.
Integration tests for collectors using recorded fixtures (deploy events, config snapshots, metrics responses). Includes CI gating and flake mitigation.
PM requirements: minimum useful incident context bundle, UX expectations for readability in Slack, and rollout constraints (avoid noise, respect restricted incidents).
Define success metrics and experiment plan: baseline measurements, adoption targets, and weekly reporting cadence for SRE leadership.
Launch plan and feature flagging: staged rollout to on-call rotations, monitoring of bot health, and rollback criteria.
PR: Add collector framework (interfaces, timeouts, concurrency control) and initial scaffold for context bundle assembly. Includes unit tests and basic CI checks.
PR: Deploy collector implementation pulling recent release events and mapping them to services/regions; posts formatted summary blocks into incident threads.
PR: Config diff collector (policy/flags) with redaction and allowlisted keys; includes examples and reviewer discussion about sensitive fields.
PR: Saturation snapshot collector integrating with metrics backend; adds links to dashboards and includes fallback behavior when metrics are delayed.
PR: Slack formatting improvements for readability (compact blocks, collapse noisy sections, consistent timestamps) and rate limiting to avoid thread spam.
PR: Restricted-mode posting (sensitive incidents): post minimal metadata to #incidents and full bundle to a restricted channel; includes config and docs.
PR: Collector caching and memoization keyed by incident + time window to reduce load; includes performance benchmarks and cache invalidation notes.
PR: Integration test harness using recorded fixtures for deploy/config/metrics; adds CI job and flake triage notes in the PR discussion.
PR: Improve error handling and partial bundle rendering (clear per-collector error sections, retry hints) so responders trust missing data signals.
PR: Add “suspected change” heuristic: highlights deploy/config deltas that overlap with start of degradation window; includes guardrails to avoid overclaiming.
PR: Emit standardized deploy annotation events from release pipeline into the platform event stream; includes schema versioning and back-compat notes.
PR: Add config snapshot endpoint/service for effective routing policy retrieval (region-aware) used by config diff collector.
PR: Add saturation dashboards (queue depth, GPU pressure, throttling) and alert rules aligned with the new saturation standard; includes reviewer feedback on thresholds.
PR: Extend SLO toolkit to support change annotations overlay in generated dashboards; includes examples and release notes.
PR: Add “recent changes” links into existing incident dashboard views (deploys/config events) and improve correlation panels.
PR: Cardinality guardrails for saturation metrics (label normalization, sampling strategy), prompted by collector scale tests.
PR: Feature flags and rollout configuration (per-channel enablement, per-service toggles); includes rollout plan checklist in the PR description.
PR: Docs updates and examples for on-call responders; links to Confluence runbook and adds a “how to request additional context” command.
Incident thread where responders request ‘recent deploys’ context; bot posts an early prototype bundle and SREs provide formatting/accuracy feedback.
Incident thread highlighting missing config diff context; follow-up discussion about which config keys are safe to post and where redaction is needed.
On-call feedback thread: proposed default time windows (last 2 deploys vs last 60 minutes) and noise concerns; includes quick poll and decision.
SRE planning thread coordinating Phase 1 rollout, owners, and success metrics; links to Linear project issue and a Drive checklist.
Platform thread debating best source-of-truth for effective routing config snapshots; includes tradeoffs between API call vs event-sourced snapshots.
Infra thread: how to expose release pipeline metadata consistently (service naming, region tags); includes example payload and validation steps.
Release engineering thread: adding deploy events and mapping commit/PR links; includes discussion of edge cases (manual rollbacks, hotfixes).
Thread about saturation metrics quality: missing labels and high-cardinality concerns; observability engineers propose a normalization strategy.
General engineering thread announcing the incident bot collectors beta and how to report issues; includes a feature-flag enablement snippet.
Postmortem follow-up thread: action items mapped to collectors; debate about ‘suspected change’ heuristics and avoiding misleading conclusions.
Incident thread where bot fails partially due to metrics lag; responders discuss desired fail-open behavior and clearer error sections.
Thread coordinating a small game-day to validate collectors under load; includes scenarios and timing (deploy during synthetic latency spike).
Thread about restricted-mode posting for customer-sensitive incidents; includes compliance concerns and proposed channel allowlist.
Security review thread on redaction/audit logging for incident bot outputs; includes requested changes before broad rollout.
Thread reviewing MTTR baseline metrics and how to measure ‘time-to-suspect-change’; includes links to dashboards and weekly reporting cadence.
Incident thread where bot correctly identifies a recent config change; responders confirm rollback path and mark the bot output as ‘useful’ feedback.
Thread about alert tuning once saturation signals go live; includes proposed thresholds and paging policy updates.
On-call rotation thread: rollout checklist and who’s opted into beta; includes brief notes from responders after first week.
Thread tracking a dependency: config snapshot endpoint performance and caching; includes quick benchmark results and next steps.
Thread planning the go/no-go for general availability: criteria, rollback plan, and comms to #eng and #incidents.
Incident thread used as a validation case for the ‘recent deploy’ collector, including debate about whether canary deploys should be highlighted differently.
Thread about adding additional deploy metadata (rollout phase, canary percentage) to improve incident context quality; includes agreement on schema changes.
Working notes: MVP definition, examples of ‘good’ vs ‘noisy’ bundles, open questions, and early responder feedback snippets.
Sheet-style doc with baseline MTTR and toil metrics by incident type/region; includes methodology notes and weekly tracking plan.
Working audit of saturation metrics coverage and quality (missing labels, cardinality hotspots), with proposed remediation steps and owners.
Draft dashboard layout/wireframe and panel list for change correlation; includes notes on what responders want above-the-fold.
Rollout checklist (feature flags, channel allowlists, monitoring, on-call enablement, comms) used during phased deployment.
Game-day plan: scenarios, timing, success criteria, observers, and how feedback will be recorded (links to Slack threads and Linear tasks).
Customer ticket: intermittent latency spikes after a rollout; includes environment/region details, logs, and links to incident thread where improved deploy context is requested.
Customer ticket: increased 429s/throttling during peak hours; investigation centers on saturation signals and queue depth; results feed into saturation collector requirements.
Customer ticket: suspected routing policy change caused errors; highlights need for safe config diffs and redaction; includes cross-links to internal tracking.
Internal support issue: incident bot posting too verbose in #incidents; request to add compact formatting and rate limiting; links to incident-bot PRs.
Email thread (SRE leadership + exec/eng leadership) summarizing plan, risks, rollout stages, and requested approvals for broader enablement.
Email thread aligning reliability program reporting: MTTR/toil metrics, weekly cadence, and how incident bot improvements will be tracked and presented to leadership.
